# Clean room and licences

pysacd was built so that nobody has to worry about where its code came from.

## No Philips/ISO reference code, anywhere

The MPEG-4 reference DST decoder isn't GPL-compatible. That includes code
derived from it, such as sacd-ripper's `libdstdec`. It has never been in this
repository, its history, its issues or its CI, and contributors may not read
it (see [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md)).

## How DST decoding was built

`csrc/dstdec.c` starts from FFmpeg's DST decoder by Peter Ross (LGPL-2.1+).
FFmpeg's decoder lacks segmentation, general mapping and the full validity
checks. Those were added through a **two-agent clean room**:

1. One agent studied the reference and wrote a prose specification, with no
   code: [dst-bitstream.md](dst-bitstream.md).
2. A second agent, which never saw the reference, implemented from that
   document alone.

The handoff document is in the repository, so anyone can audit what crossed
the wall. Section 7 of it lists every behaviour that differs from FFmpeg.
Section 8 records the errata found later by black-box testing.

## sacd_extract only as a black box

`sacd_extract` is used as a compiled oracle to compare output against,
locally and in CI, where it is built from a pinned upstream commit. Its source
is never copied or paraphrased into this repository. Where pysacd matches its
behaviour (file names, DSDIFF layout, `-P` text), the behaviour was
established by running the binary and comparing output.

## Licences

| Part | Licence |
|---|---|
| pysacd as a whole | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `csrc/dstdec.c` | LGPL-2.1-or-later (FFmpeg's header kept), which is GPL-compatible |
| libFLAC (optional, for FLAC output) | BSD-3-Clause |
| mutagen (optional, for tagging) | GPL-2.0-or-later |

New code is GPL-2.0-or-later. No dependency or copied code under incompatible
terms may be added.

## Acknowledgements

- **[sacd-ripper](https://github.com/sacd-ripper/sacd-ripper)**: the
  Scarletbook layouts and `sacd_extract`'s behaviour, which pysacd reproduces.
  Its compiled binary was the oracle throughout.
- **FFmpeg's DST decoder** by Peter Ross (LGPL-2.1+), the base of
  `csrc/dstdec.c`.
- **[MusicBrainz](https://musicbrainz.org)** and the **Cover Art Archive**,
  for tags and covers.
- The **PS3 SACD Ripper** homebrew, whose protocol pysacd speaks.
